chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ibn Abi Najran from Muthanna al-Hannat from Zurara who said:
I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the testimony of women, is it valid in marriage? He said, 'Yes, and it is not valid in divorce.'
And he said, 'Ali (peace be upon him) said, 'The testimony of women is valid in stoning if they are three men and two women, and if there are four women and two men, it is not valid in stoning.''
I said, 'Is the testimony of women valid with men in blood (diyah)?' He said, 'No.'
ai.seo_question: What are the rules for the validity of women's testimony in marriage, divorce, and stoning according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details Imam al-Sadiq’s (AS) nuanced application of testimony rules, linking the prohibition of women's testimony in divorce to the specific legal mechanism of *talaq* rather than general witness validity. It further clarifies the complex jurisprudential debate regarding stoning (*rجم*), citing Imam Ali’s (AS) view that mixed-gender panels are invalid for this specific punishment, while explicitly excluding women from testimony in blood money (*diyah*) cases. This reflects the Shia scholarly tradition of distinguishing between different types of legal acts (*fiqh al-af'al*) and their respective evidentiary requirements.
